summary: Grassy Hill tower in Franklin County is listed as gone; no source describes it. The hilltop is now a public DCR natural area preserve.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone. The hilltop is now a state natural area preserve.

access.note: Natural area preserve open to visitors on marked trails, with closures for deer hunting and on some dates.

visit.trail_note: Five miles of hiking trails; visitors must stay on marked trails. Deer hunting closes the West Loop Trail and areas west of the Connector Trail from September 15, 2026 to January 3, 2027.

notes_for_editor: Only the Association's list says a tower existed here and is gone. No source read gives its build year, height, staffing, owner or removal date, so the story leaves those out. The list point (37.0243, -79.8936) is about 3 km northeast of the preserve's Wikipedia coordinates (37.006, -79.92), so the record may mean a different spot or hill; the story assumes it is this hill, which is likely but not confirmed. Acreage conflicts: the trail guide gives 1,295 acres and the Wikipedia article gives 1,440; the story does not use acreage. The DCR page links a 'Telecommunication Towers (PDF)' document, which was not located or read and is the best next lead for any tower on the preserve. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced by public, from DCR's own pages.
